comments.why_zh: 问答谈的是通过让项目在技术上保持简单来完成 Braid。

> 问：你说过在 Braid 之前你做过很多项目，但都没能真正完成。Braid 有什么特别之处，让你完成了它？

comments.text: TFA has some good points. I'd go even further on the situation where you quit your job to work on an indie game -- if you ever find yourself doing this, and you've never built a game by yourself before, you'd better have several years of runway. For many years one of my favorite talks about indie games development was Jonathan Blow's speech at UC Berkeley CSUA (2011) ( [LINK] ) Initially I loved his main message during the talk: "You have to be brutally effective to finish a project in a reasonable amount of time." But there's a part in the Q&A that later grew to be even more poignant to me: [VIDEO] > Q: You said you worked on many projects before Braid which didn't quite get completed. What was special about Braid which made you complete it? > A: What was special was it had been a long time since I'd finished anything on my own, and I sat down and decided that "Dammit I'm going to finish something this time". And, "To that end, so I can finish this, I'm gonna make something that is technically pretty simple"... For some of us, it's REALLY HARD to complete a side-project while working full-time job. For most of my career I had completed a real game only when it was for a job (or for a client) and I worked on it full-time. The single reason I hadn't made a game as a side project was because I'd quit before I finished. I finally figured out something that worked for me, and it was counter to all the advice I'd heard. comments.author: lackbeard
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What does mastery look like in software engineering?
comments.why_zh: 通过交付许多程序来变强，而不是狭窄地专精。
comments.quote_zh: 很久以前我看过 Jonathan Blow 的一个很好的演讲，其中他提出的一个观点真的让我产生了共鸣。
comments.text_zh: 典范级大师：John Carmack、Jeff Dean、Bram Cohen。他们做什么？我认为他们都极其擅长把事情做成。所以要聪明、努力，并极度专注于交付。很久以前我看过 Jonathan Blow 的一个很好的演讲，其中他提出的一个观点真的让我产生了共鸣。这个观点是：要擅长编程，你需要有交付大量程序的经验，因此你应该围绕尽可能多地交付好程序来优化你的职业生涯。把这和常见建议对比一下：成为数据库、分布式系统、OOP、测试或类似领域的专家……补充：找到那个演讲了：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Example masters: John Carmack, Jeff Dean, Bram Cohen. What do they do? I think they're all extremely effective at getting things done. So be smart, hard working, and laser focused on shipping. A long time ago I saw a good talk by Jonathan Blow wherein he made a point that really resonated with me. The point was that to get good at programming you need the experience of shipping a lot of programs and thus you should optimize your career around shipping as many good programs as you can. Contrast this with the common advice of being an expert in databases, or distributed systems, or OOP, or testing, or something like that... Edit: found the talk: [VIDEO]

comments.author: nlawalker
comments.why_zh: Blow 解释说先用简单数组以便交付，优化的是所需耗费的生命年数。
comments.quote_zh: 这让我想起 Jonathan Blow 演讲中的一部分[1]
comments.text_zh: 这让我想起 Jonathan Blow 演讲中的一部分[1]，他在其中从生产力的角度为这一点辩护。他解释说，他在 Braid 里几乎所有东西的初始实现都用了 arrays of records，只有在发现瓶颈之后才做修改，因为如果他应对每一个技术挑战时都试图找到最优的数据结构和算法，他就永远无法交付。“还有第三样东西[在速度和内存之外]可能是你会想优化的，它比这两者都重要得多，那就是每个程序实现所需耗费的你生命中的年数。”这当然是从一个单人独立游戏开发者的视角出发的，但这是一个很好也很有趣、值得考虑的视角。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: This reminds me of a portion of a talk Jonathan Blow gave[1], where he justifies this from a productivity angle. He explains how his initial implementation for virtually everything in Braid used arrays of records, and only after finding bottlenecks did he make changes, because if he had approached every technical challenge by trying to find the optimal data structure and algorithm he would never have shipped. "There's a third thing [beyond speed and memory] that you might want to optimize for which is much more important than either of these, which is years of your life required per program implementation." This is of course from the perspective of a solo indie game developer, but it's a good and interesting perspective to consider. [1] [VIDEO]
